name: drinks
description: Mixology and hot drinks. `mix` builds a drink in a REUSABLE vessel (tags.drinkware) out of ingredient PROFILES, never item ids; `brew` needs a hot-water appliance (furniture flags.brew_tier). A finished drink lives on the vessel's custom_data as a serving count and a quality band — you carry it, drink it down, decant it, and rinse it out. Alcohol is DERIVED from the ingredients' tags.abv and lands through the existing drug_alcohol laced path on each swallow, so intoxication behaves exactly as it does for a bottled cocktail. Cold mixing needs only a vessel in hand.

mix.note: Ungated on purpose — a vessel in hand is the whole requirement for a cold drink. Discovered through the drinkware item description.

brew.note: Hot drinks only. A declaration-only specializedAction row makes a kettle or coffee machine advertise BREW on examine.

rinse.note: Needs a sink. The 'could do with a rinse' line on the last swallow is the teaching moment.

extensionPoints: A new ingredient needs only tags.drink_profile + tags.pour_units (+ tags.abv if alcoholic) to work in every recipe its profile fits — no edit to this plugin.
A new appliance tier is one entry in config.js BREW_TIERS plus the furniture flag.
Drinkware is tags.drinkware + tags.drinkware_kind + tags.fillable (capacity in servings).
notes: LOAD ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: specialized actions fire in registration order, and `drinks` must claim `drink` before `fillable` so a cup holding a poured drink isn't treated as plain water. Alphabetical ordering already does this (d < f); the belt to that braces is the holdsDrink() guard inside plugins/fillable, which does not depend on ordering.

A vessel drink deliberately does NOT pass through applyItemUse, so it inherits none of well_fed / restore_hp / freshness / the item.consumed hook. finishServing implements thirst, sanity and alcohol only.
